title: Strict bipartite superactivation of distillable entanglement
source: Shor, Smolin, and Terhal proposed strict superactivation of bipartite distillable entanglement, in the sense of Eq.~\eqref{eq:05aa-superactivation}, and showed that it would follow from a conjecture that certain NPT Werner states are undistillable \sourcecite{ref:05aa-shor-smolin-terhal}{SST01}. After establishing multiparty superactivation, Shor, Smolin, and Thapliyal name finding bipartite states that show nonadditivity of distillable entanglement as a direction for further research \sourcecite{ref:05aa-shor-smolin-thapliyal}{SST03}. The zero-plus-zero formulation across a fixed bipartition is derived from these sources.
progress:
The distillability criterion of Horodecki, Horodecki, and Horodecki, in the Schmidt-rank-two form of Lemmas~1 and~2 of DiVincenzo et al., reads
\begin{equation}
 D_{\leftrightarrow}(\omega)>0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists\,n\geq1,\ \exists\,|v\rangle:\quad
 \operatorname{SR}_{A^n:B^n}(|v\rangle)\leq2,
 \quad
 \langle v|(\omega^{T_B})^{\otimes n}|v\rangle<0,
 \label{eq:05aa-criterion}
\end{equation}
where $|v\rangle$ ranges over unit vectors on $n$ copies and $\operatorname{SR}$ denotes Schmidt rank across the indicated bipartition. A state satisfying the condition for a given $n$ is called $n$-copy distillable. Failure of the condition for finitely many values of $n$ does not establish $D_\leftrightarrow(\omega)=0$ \sourcecite{ref:05aa-horodecki}{HHH98}, \sourcecite{ref:05aa-divincenzo-et-al}{DSS+00}.

Shor, Smolin, and Thapliyal established superactivation of bound entanglement among five separated parties: two four-party states, each undistillable because every party is separated from every other by a separable cut, combine into a state from which an EPR pair can be distilled. Their operational restrictions differ from a fixed bipartition with unrestricted operations inside each laboratory, so this does not produce a pair satisfying Eq.~\eqref{eq:05aa-superactivation} \sourcecite{ref:05aa-shor-smolin-thapliyal}{SST03}.

comment: The all-copy NPT undistillability question remains unresolved in the literature checked through 15 September 2026, and therefore so does strict bipartite superactivation of $D_\leftrightarrow$. By Eq.~\eqref{eq:05aa-equivalence}, the question is equivalent to the unrestricted question of the record on \href{https://qiqc-op.com/problem/op_74c4ffb5b042baf2/}{NPT bound entanglement and the rank-five frontier}, which additionally asks whether a counterexample can have rank five and records further finite-copy progress. An affirmative answer requires one fixed NPT state that fails Eq.~\eqref{eq:05aa-criterion} for every $n$; a negative answer amounts to proving that every NPT state is distillable. The two-copy Werner result is finite-copy progress, not an all-copy zero-rate certificate. Multipartite superactivation and activation of an already distillable NPT state do not settle the question. The record on \href{https://qiqc-op.com/problem/op_fc663252f5664f40/}{zero two-way quantum capacity of endpoint Holevo--Werner channels} asks whether the Werner state at the one-copy undistillability threshold is undistillable in every dimension $d\geq3$; a proof for a single $d$ would already give a pair satisfying Eq.~\eqref{eq:05aa-superactivation}.
